There is real print and real handwriting on the spines, the labels and the tabs, but the camera is oblique and the aperture wide, so only one notebook edge near the middle of the frame is sharp and every spine and label softens out of focus; the lettering stays visible as lettering that will not resolve, never wiped blank and never smeared. Materials carry the picture: warm wood grain and one old ring mark, the fibrous cut edges of paper, glazed ceramic, dulled wire binding, a little dust along the shelf lip. Light: one window off to the left gives soft directional daylight that grazes the paper edges and throws honest soft shadows to the right; nothing else is lit. Composition: horizontal frame shot from a low oblique angle so the spines recede, everything off-centre and irregular, no line-up and no grid - but keep the densest, most interesting cluster of notebooks and tabs in the middle third of the frame, because the picture will be cropped to a wide strip and may also be cropped to a narrow upright slice from the centre.
